statement: The per-fire regression cost is not a small constant: at the densest late gate (contest.gate) a single fire re-evaluates 26 earlier controls, and the count rises with the gate's depth in the sprint (6 at survey.gate). This is measured from a real dense ledger, not estimated.

downgrades.why: a single dense ledger; the exact counts vary with a sprint's control density and with review retries that inflate late fires.

would_change: Ledgers from several profiles showing the late-gate regression count staying a small constant regardless of depth.

statement: Total regression work grows superlinearly (quadratically) in the number of gates, not linearly: the loop re-runs every earlier control unconditionally, so the aggregate is a triangular sum over gates. In the measured run 239 regression verdicts dominate all grading. The prior belief that re-runs are 'cheap and negligible' is refuted; H-1 and H-3 (bounded per-fire) do not survive, H-2 does.

downgrades.why: the quadratic aggregate is derived from per-gate measurements plus the code's unconditional re-run, not read off a single recorded total-work metric.

would_change: Gate code that filtered the regression set (keep-best or current-macro only), which would break the triangular sum and make the aggregate linear.
